conventions.convention: Dimensions satisfy d ≥ 1; flows are finite compositions of global C¹ diffeomorphisms between nonempty open subsets of the same Euclidean dimension.
Base densities are nonnegative extended-real Lebesgue-measurable functions of integral one. Model measures are specified on Borel sets by inverse images, assuming Countable Choice.
Density transformation uses the absolute determinant of the inverse derivative; the density is a version, and logarithms involve nonzero derivative determinants.

Conditional factors are positive and continuous everywhere, factorize p pointwise, and have jointly C¹ conditional CDFs with positive first derivative and slices bijective onto (0,1). Conditional inverses hold preceding coordinates fixed.

load_bearing.statement: Assuming Countable Choice, for a C¹ diffeomorphism T:U→V between nonempty open subsets of Rᵈ and a Lebesgue probability density p_U, q(x)=p_U(T⁻¹(x))|det D(T⁻¹)(x)| is Lebesgue measurable and integrates over every Borel B⊆V to the transformed measure μ_U(T⁻¹(B)). For finite compositions, the forward and inverse log absolute Jacobian determinants add over the corresponding stages.

A finite composition T=T_K∘⋯∘T_1 of global C¹ diffeomorphisms between open subsets of Rᵈ is a normalizing flow. A base density is Lebesgue measurable, nonnegative and of integral one; assuming Countable Choice, its model measure on Borel B⊆V is μ_X(B)=μ_U(T⁻¹(B)).

published_dependencies.used_for: The explicit choice assumption carried by the measure construction, change-of-variables theorem, box-volume theorem and all assigned probabilistic claims.
Total differentiability, continuous derivative matrices and local C¹ inverses.
Constructing base, transformed and interval measures by integrating nonnegative measurable densities.
Lebesgue measurability of Borel sets under Countable Choice.
Measurability of transported level sets and preimages under inverse diffeomorphisms.
Jacobian determinants and the absolute volume scale factor.
Continuity of determinants of continuous derivative matrices.
Derivative products for compositions and inverse identities.
Products of stage determinants and their nonvanishing.
Measurability of density products and indicator restrictions, including extended nonnegative values.
Applying change of variables to the inverse map and a restricted base density.
The conditional-CDF determinant and both affine coupling determinants.
Local C¹ inverses patched by global bijectivity of the triangular CDF map.
Normalization of uniform densities on the unit cube and unit interval, and Borel measurability of the segment.
Well-definedness of the line-supported image probability measure.
Every flow density assigns zero mass to the null segment, even if its density takes infinite values.
